old_title: Strictly's Shirley and Anton set for surprise week three dance off - live
new_title: Strictly Come Dancing's Delta Goodrem lands first 9 of the series - live

Another Saturday means another brand new episode of Strictly Come Dancing, with more show stopping routines, more sequins and more fake tans - we wouldn't have it any other way.
Last week's episode saw the celebrities and the professional dance partners take to the stage to perform to tracks from Hollywood movies, marking the earliest point that Movie Week has ever occurred in the show's schedule.
Hairdresser Chris Appleton and his professional partner Amy Dowden were the first couple to leave the show, after the judges chose to back Jaime Winston and Carlos Gu in the dance off.
This time around, there's no set theme, meaning that we'll be treated to everything from a Charleston to Gina G (yes, really) to a quickstep to "I'm a Believer".
And judges Shirley Ballas and Anton du Beke will be getting in on the action with a surprise dance off of their own during Sunday night's results show.
They'll be briefly swapping the judging panel for the dancefloor when they take part in a ballroom versus Latin showdown as part of a special group dance with the Strictly pros.
Ballas, of course, is representing Team Latin, while Du Beke is firmly on Team Ballroom.
And with the season now in its third week, there are still criticisms from fans over the new presenting trio.
Last week's results show saw proceedings get a bit of a shake-up, with Emma Willis joining Johannes Radebe to debrief with the judges. Fans seemed to react positively to this Emma-Jojo combo - could the show bosses be gearing up to test out yet more iterations to see what works best?
We'll be keeping you updated in the run-up to the show and during the episode itself...
What time is Strictly on tonight?
Good afternoon and welcome to The Independent's live blog for tonight's episode of Strictly Come Dancing.
The competition is now in its third week, with Chris Appleton and Amy Dowden being in the unenviable position of being the first couple to leave the series last Sunday.
As ever, the big question for the afternoon is: what time do things kick off this evening? As with last week, the show will be kicking off at 6.15pm on BBC One and BBC iPlayer.

Another Saturday meant another brand new episode of Strictly Come Dancing, with more show-stopping routines, more sequins and more fake tans - we wouldn't have it any other way.
With no theme, week three delivered a truly eclectic collection of dances, including a Charleston to Gina G (yes, really) and a quickstep to "I'm a Believer". And there was a huge range when it came to the scoring too, with 18 points between the best- and worst-performing celebrities.
At the top of the leaderboard, Delta Goodrem scored 33 for her Disco-themed Salsa, which landed the first nine of the series from Motsi Mabuse.
Cach Mercer also impressed with his ambitious Couple's Choice set to Raye's "Beware... The South London Lover Boy" before Tabby Stoecker closed the show with a sensual Argentine Tango that left Craig Revel Horwood almost speechless.
At the other end of the leaderboard, and possibly in trouble in tomorrow's results show, were Melanie Walters - who struggled to master the Charleston - and Shaun Wright-Phillips, whose quickstep didn't include many quick steps.
Follow all the latest updates below...
That's a wrap!
One more order of business: it's Anton who will have the casting vote in tomorrow's results show.
But who will be in the dance-off? You can get your votes in now on the BBC website to help decide.
I'll be back next week for another action-packed live show!
Tabby's scores are in...
And they're good!
Tabby has received an 8, 8, 7 and an 8 - for a total of 31.
Ok, I can see why that routine was chosen to close the show. Wow.
Here's what the judges have made of it...
Craig: "Love, love, love."
Motsi: "I loved it, I had goosebumps. You are the dark horse here. You are great."
Shirley: "It was extremely steamy and very sensual. This is on a very good track."
Anton: "To coin a phrase from an old friend of mine... 'love, love, love'."
Closing the show, it's Tabby and Mark... and it's Argentine Tango time!
Tabby and newbie pro Mark are dancing to Ariana Grande's "hate that I made you love me". And they are bringing the fire...
Bethany's scores are in...
It's 6, 7, 7 and 7 - a very respectable total of 27.
Aw, that was lovely! Very summery, which I appreciate in this weather.
The judges are now giving their verdicts...
Anton: "I enjoyed it enormously. You've got a wonderful frame and a perfect head position. Moving forward, I would just like a bit more musicality."
Craig: "The transitions were a little bit messy. I thought you could cover the floor more. But I really loved it."
Motsi: "I wanted more and you got that really well done. You guys are so clean, I love that. Everything gets lighter when you dance. Very nice."
Shirley: "Musicality, I enjoyed. All in all, for week three, I thought this was extremely impressive and you should both be proud of yourselves."
Two couples to go!
It's Bethany and Nancy up now, with an American Smooth to "Love Song" by Sara Bareilles. I love seeing how the same-sex couples approach the routines that are mainly danced in hold. They get to have so much more fun with it!
John's scores are in...
It's a 4 (ouch!), 5, 5 and a 6 - a total of 20.
Here's the judges' feedback for John...
Shirley: "What I found is the coordination now starts to get better. You've got some good leading skills going on there. I was pleasantly surprised by your first Latin number."
Anton: "I liked it a lot. It felt like it's almost there. If you had another week on this, it would have been a great dance. I think you'll become really good at this because there's a lot to like."
Craig: "I thought too cool, too laidback, not much was happening. It was a bit dull for my liking.
Motsi: "I think the vibe was cool... I think you brought the vibe, I also felt like you were very vulnerable. I would like you to work on Cuban motion and how you move across."
Cha Cha-ing into week three, it's John and Katya.
I loved their Titanic-themed Movie Week performance, though the judges weren't so keen with Craig giving them just four points and the whole panel awarding a total score of 23.
This week they're dancing to Justin Timberlake's "Rock Your Body".
